facts.text: Avon’s name comes from the Celtic word for river, echoing the English settlers who named many towns after familiar English rivers.
The town was originally part of the Connecticut Western Reserve and saw its first permanent settlers arrive in 1814 from Montgomery County, New York.
Avon became an incorporated city in 1961 after evolving from a village that had formed in 1917.
Avon Middle School earned national recognition as a Blue Ribbon school in 2020, highlighting the city’s commitment to academic excellence.
The local branch of the Lorain Public Library is expanding, adding 16,000 square feet after a 2020 levy, making it a growing cultural hub.
Geographically, Avon sits in northeastern Ohio’s rolling terrain just a short drive from Lake Erie, which shapes its mild, lake‑influenced climate.
